rules.title: CTFE-evaluable expression forms
rules.statement: Compile-time constant evaluation accepts exactly: integer/float/bool/string literals, parenthesized expressions (transparent), unary expressions, binary expressions, and bare identifier references (VAR_REF) resolvable to a const. Any other expression form is not a compile-time constant and is rejected.

rules.title: Integer literal kind from suffix
rules.statement: An integer literal must be well-formed; its CTFE kind is its explicit integer suffix kind (e.g. i32, u64) if present, else the polymorphic IntLit. Its value is parsed as a 64-bit integer (both signed and unsigned views retained).

rules.title: Float literal kind from suffix; underscores stripped
rules.statement: A float literal must be well-formed; underscore separators are removed before parsing. Its CTFE kind is its explicit float suffix kind (f32/f64) if present, else the polymorphic FloatLit.

rules.title: Bool literal value
rules.statement: A bool literal evaluates to kind Bool; its value is true iff its stored byte is nonzero.

rules.title: String literal CTFE representation
rules.statement: A string literal evaluates with kind Slice (a stand-in for str / Slice<u8>); the literal's actual &str/Slice<u8> typeref is validated separately by the caller.
rules.uncertainty: Slice kind is a CTFE-internal stand-in; the actual surface type check happens outside this unit.

rules.title: Unary '-' requires numeric operand
rules.statement: Unary '-' negates an integer or float operand (preserving its kind); applied to any non-numeric operand it is rejected.

rules.title: Unary '!' requires bool operand
rules.statement: Unary '!' logically negates a Bool operand; applied to any non-bool operand it is rejected. (No bitwise-not on integers in CTFE.)
rules.uncertainty: Bitwise '!' on integers is not handled here; only bool is accepted.

rules.title: && and || require bool operands
rules.statement: Binary '&&' and '||' require both operands to be Bool and yield Bool; otherwise rejected.

rules.title: Integer kind promotion in binary ops
rules.statement: For an integer binop, the result kind is the promotion of the two operand kinds: equal kinds stay; a polymorphic IntLit yields to the other operand's kind; otherwise the result is I64.
rules.uncertainty: Mixed concrete-int kinds (e.g. i32 op u32) fall back to I64 rather than a Rust-style type error.

rules.title: Integer arithmetic/comparison uses result-kind signedness
rules.statement: Integer +,-,*,/,%,comparisons are computed using signed semantics iff the promoted result kind is signed, else unsigned; both signed and unsigned representations of the result are kept.

rules.title: Division/modulo by zero is a CTFE error
rules.statement: Integer '/' or '%' with a zero divisor, and float '/' with a zero divisor, are rejected as compile-time errors (no panic, no UB at CTFE).

rules.title: Shift amount masked to 6 bits
rules.statement: Integer '<<' and '>>' mask the shift amount to its low 6 bits (& 63). '<<' is computed unsigned; '>>' is arithmetic when the result kind is signed, logical otherwise.
rules.uncertainty: Mask 63 assumes a 64-bit shift width regardless of operand bit-width (e.g. u8).

rules.title: Mixed int/float binop coerces to float
rules.statement: When either operand of an arithmetic/comparison binop is a float, integer operands are coerced to double; result kind is F64 if either side is F64, else F32 if either is F32, else FloatLit.

rules.title: Bool equality comparisons
rules.statement: Binary '==' and '!=' on two Bool operands compare their values and yield Bool.

rules.title: Parenthesized expression is transparent
rules.statement: A parenthesized expression evaluates to its inner expression's CTFE value (no effect on kind or value).

rules.title: Identifier resolves to const RHS via resolver
rules.statement: A bare identifier in const-eval position (VAR_REF) is resolved, when a resolver is supplied, to the named const's RHS expression and its owning holder, then evaluated recursively; cross-package consts resolve provided the resolver knows them. Without a resolver, or if unresolved, the identifier is not a compile-time constant.
